title: Mars Window Go/No-Go Readiness Review
summary: Follow-up readiness review three weeks after the July program review. Status: tile microcracking root cause confirmed as supplier sintering issue, reverted supplier tiles installing on all five ships; docking seal passed 214 cryo cycles, propellant transfer demo confirmed for Flight 14 on September 2; Pad B plumbing mod on schedule; FAA dual-launch approval received in writing. Optimus payload freeze signed on schedule. New risks: Ship 4 engine bay harness rework and a two-week slip in the Mars relay constellation deployment. Go/no-go poll set for October 20.
decisions: Flight 14 with the full ship-to-ship propellant transfer demo is confirmed for September 2
Ship 4 harness rework proceeds without moving the ship order; Ship 5 becomes the spare if it slips
Mars relay constellation deployment slip is acceptable; landing coverage is preserved even with six of eight relays
Formal go/no-go poll for the tanker campaign is October 20
The Taylor Swift livestream load-test learnings on X are shared with the landing-broadcast team

action_items.task: Complete Ship 4 engine bay harness rework and re-run integrated checkout
Publish the tanker campaign schedule with pad assignments to the whole program
Get the honest Mars comms bandwidth number to the X broadcast team and MrBeast's producers
Brief NASA on the updated flight schedule before Flight 14

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Okay, three weeks since the program review, ninety-four days to the window opening. This is the meeting where we find out if the July decisions actually happened or just got agreed to. Mark — tiles. You owed me a root cause with samples, and you delivered a report I actually read twice. Walk Gwynne through the punchline.

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: Punchline: it was the supplier's sintering profile, not the material. The new supplier ran a shorter sintering cycle to hit our rate demands, which left residual porosity, which becomes microcracking under thermal cycling. So the July decision to revert suppliers on critical zones was right, and better — the original supplier reviewed the data and found they can lift their rate twenty percent with a second kiln, so the two-week schedule hit we budgeted is now four days.

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: And installation status: reverted tiles are on Ships 1 and 2 completely, Ship 3 is sixty percent, Ships 4 and 5 start next week. The kiln surge covers all five with nine days of margin. Tiles have officially left my top-three worry list, which is a sentence I want framed.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Frame it next to the seal data. Speaking of which — the quick-disconnect. I said two hundred cryo cycles. What happened?

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: Two hundred and fourteen cycles, zero leaks, and we kept going past your gate on purpose — the redesigned seal is now the most-tested component on the vehicle. We tore down unit three after cycle two hundred and the preload shim showed four percent wear, well inside margin. The transfer demo hardware is installed on both Flight 14 vehicles. I'm calling it: September 2, we fly the demo.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: September 2 confirmed. That demo working changes everything downstream — the tanker campaign, NASA's confidence, frankly the President's statement gets a lot easier to stand behind. Gwynne, speaking of things in writing — FAA.

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: In writing, received Tuesday. Dual-launch operations approved — both pads active in the same window, up to one launch per eighteen hours combined during the campaign period. No supplemental noise assessment required; they accepted the Flight 12 acoustic data. I want to note for the record that the licensing office turned this around in three weeks, which is the fastest I've seen in twenty years, so whatever is happening in Washington, it's working.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Good — and the fast-track energy pilot got announced last week too, so Washington is having a productive summer by its standards. Pad B plumbing mod, still on schedule? We took it down on the 10th.

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: Down on the 10th as planned, the deluge decoupling is forty percent done, back online September 1 — one day before the demo flight, which is tight but the demo flies from Pad A anyway. Once B is back, we run a wet dress on it before it enters the campaign rotation. And with the FAA letter in hand I can finally publish the full tanker schedule with pad assignments to the program, which I'll do by the 20th. Three thousand people are about to see their October.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Publish it. People fight harder for a schedule they can see. Okay — Optimus. For the record, because I know it got noticed: the freeze spec got signed on the 15th, by me, no drive-by upgrades, and the Tesla review yesterday confirmed the flight units are building to the frozen spec with the Mars delta package. Thirty robots plus six spares, first ten arrive at Starbase September 5 for vibration and integration testing.

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: And I want to publicly appreciate that you froze your own upgrade authority, because the payload mass hasn't moved in four weeks and my structures team has stopped flinching when you visit. Now — my turn to bring bad news, because this meeting was going suspiciously well. Two new items. Ship 4's engine bay harness failed continuity checks on eleven circuits during integrated checkout. It's a manufacturing defect in a harness batch — chafing at the bulkhead pass-throughs. Rework is eighteen days.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Eighteen days puts Ship 4 done by, what, September 10? Window opens mid-November. Where does that eat margin?

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: It eats Ship 4's own margin, not the campaign's — but it means if anything else goes wrong on Ship 4 specifically, it misses the window. My proposal: don't reshuffle the ship order, just formally designate Ship 5 as the swing spare. If Ship 4 slips again, we fly four ships and Ship 5's payload gets redistributed. The mission architecture already tolerates four; you said it in July — we'd rather fly five that all work.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Agreed — no reshuffle, Ship 5 is the designated spare, and check the harness batch traceability on every other ship today, because manufacturing defects travel in packs. What's the second item?

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: The Mars relay constellation. The eight comms relay satellites that give us landing telemetry and imagery — the last two slipped two weeks because their launch shares a pad rotation with the tanker campaign prep. The question you'll get asked, including by your broadcast friends, is what coverage looks like if we fly with six relays instead of eight.

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: Answer: six of eight preserves continuous telemetry during entry, descent and landing for all five ships — the two we'd lose are the redundancy pair that also doubles imagery downlink. So with six, we get the landings live in telemetry, but the good pictures come down over hours instead of minutes. Mission-wise it's fine. Broadcast-wise, the twenty-minute-delay live imagery show becomes a next-day show.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Which is exactly the honest answer I owe the X broadcast team and Jimmy's producers by the 26th — I'll give them both scenarios so they design two formats. I am not letting a content plan put schedule pressure on a launch campaign; that conversation only ever goes one direction. The relays fly when they fly.

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: Thank you for saying that out loud in this room, and I'm going to hold you to it in November when the producers are calling. Related, actually — the X team's load test for the Taylor Swift stream, whatever comes of that deal, is testing thirty-million-concurrent live video. The landing broadcast rides the same infrastructure. Whatever they learn in that test, our broadcast team should get, because the landing could triple that number.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Good catch — I'll connect the two teams this week, one learning pipeline instead of two. Okay, the big one. Go/no-go structure. The tanker campaign is the commit point — once we start filling depots, we're spending ships and propellant against the clock. When do we poll?

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: October 20. By then we have the demo flown and analyzed, Pad B back in rotation with a wet dress, Ship 4 rework proven out one way or the other, and the first robots through vibration testing. We poll every system lead formally — actual go/no-go, recorded, the full ritual. If it's go, first tanker flies October 24. And Elon — at that poll, everyone gets to vote their system honestly, including saying no-go to your face. I want to hear you say that sentence.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: Anyone can no-go at the poll, to my face, and the only thing that gets them in trouble is saying go when they meant no. I've buried enough hardware to mean that. October 20, formal poll, October 24 first tanker. Mark, last thing — the entry instrumentation. Still surviving the mass diet?

transcript.speaker: Mark Juncosa
transcript.text: Untouched, per your July order — full pressure taps and thermal mapping on all five ships. If Mars entry surprises us, we'll know exactly how. And if it doesn't surprise us, we'll have the aero database that makes the 2028 crewed decision an engineering question instead of a courage question.

transcript.speaker: Elon Musk
transcript.text: That's the whole point. Alright — summary for the record. Tiles: root cause confirmed, reverted, ahead of schedule. Seal: two hundred fourteen cycles, demo confirmed September 2. FAA: approved in writing. Pad B: back September 1. Optimus: frozen, first units at Starbase September 5. Ship 4: harness rework, Ship 5 designated spare, batch traceability check today. Relays: six-of-eight is acceptable, broadcast gets the honest number. Go/no-go poll October 20, first tanker October 24. Ninety-four days. This is the best program review I've ever sat in, which means everyone should go find what we missed.

transcript.speaker: Gwynne Shotwell
transcript.text: Already scheduled — failure-hunt week starts Monday, every system lead red-teams someone else's system. And Elon, one personal note: whatever happens in November, this team has already done something nobody else on Earth can do. Tell them that on Friday. Then land the ships.
